sector: Industrials / Diversified small-cap (Memorialization + Industrial Technologies/EV-battery process + SGK Brand Solutions)
industry: Specialty Industrial conglomerate (bronze/granite memorials + caskets, dry-electrode calendering for Li-ion batteries, brand/packaging services)
drawdown_context: MATW entered the cutoff window at ~$20.7 (down ~34% from trailing 52-week high) into a multi-front distressed-restructuring tape: (1) FY24 GAAP net loss of $(59.7)M vs FY23 net income $39.1M; (2) refinanced 5.25% unsecured 2025 notes into 8.625% senior secured SECOND-LIEN 2027 notes in Sept 2024 -- textbook distressed-pricing refinancing; (3) Tesla litigation actively expanding (June 2024 trade-secrets complaint + Feb 13, 2025 second complaint on patent inventorship in dry battery electrode -- 6% of FY24 sales); (4) activist proxy contest in early 2025 ($4.9M of legal fees through H1 FY25); (5) announced Jan 7, 2025 deal to contribute SGK Brand Solutions into a JV with Southern Graphics for $250M cash + $50M preferred + 40% common, shrinking the company by ~30% of sales; (6) ATM equity shelf filed March 11, 2025 (1.25M shares).

rfm_tuples.R: [FY24 net loss attributable to Matthews] $(59,660); [FY23] $39,136; [FY22] $(99,828). Sales $1,795.7M FY24 vs $1,880.9M FY23 (-4.5% YoY). Adjusted EBITDA $205.2M FY24 vs $225.8M FY23 (-9.1%). Industrial Technologies segment EBITDA fell 40% YoY ($66.3M -> $39.7M).
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: existence check. Did the company in fact post a GAAP net loss for the second time in three years (FY22 and FY24) on declining revenue and falling segment EBITDA -- consistent with deteriorating intrinsic franchise rather than a sentiment markdown?
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Item 7 MD&A + Item 8 Consolidated Statements of Operations
rfm_tuples.M_value: Confirmed: GAAP loss $(59.7)M in FY24; Industrial Tech (the EV-battery-tooling growth story) cratered -40% EBITDA YoY on customer delays + Tesla dispute. SGK Brand Solutions EBITDA up only $4.5M off a flat top-line. Memorialization EBITDA basically flat. FY24 included $33.6M of goodwill+asset writedowns ($16.7M Surfaces & Engineering goodwill to zero, $13.7M held-for-sale impairment, $3.1M cost-method investment).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms franchise impairment, not just sentiment. The Industrial Tech segment -- the entire growth story sold to public-market investors (dry-electrode for Li-ion) -- broke. Loss is real, not driven solely by one-timers.

rfm_tuples.R: In September 2024, the Company issued $300.0 million aggregate principal amount of 8.625% senior secured second lien notes due October 1, 2027... [proceeds] used to redeem all of the Company's outstanding 5.25% senior unsecured notes due December 1, 2025... [Domestic revolver] amended and restated in September 2024.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: distressed_debt_refi. (A) 8.625% senior SECURED SECOND-LIEN replacing 5.25% senior UNSECURED is a 337 bps spread blowout AND a covenant ratchet. (B) What was the trigger that prevented a normal unsecured refi? Compare to ANDE's First Amendment which was post-acquisition documentation.
rfm_tuples.M_source: 10-K Notes 5/12 Debt and Financing + Q2 FY25 10-Q Note 7
rfm_tuples.M_value: Distressed refi terms: 8.625% coupon vs prior 5.25% (Fed Funds Sept 2024 = 4.75-5.00%, so this is a real credit-spread blowout above benchmark); security upgrade UNSECURED -> SECOND-LIEN SECURED is the classic 'collateralize when cushion gone' signal; total LTD $769M vs TTM Adj EBITDA $205M = 3.75x leverage; revolver drew from $410.5M (9/30/24) to $495.0M (3/31/25) = +$85M into the trough; $4.9M financing fees indicate limited-buyer process.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Textbook Mode A distress tell. A non-distressed mid-cap industrial refi would have rolled 5.25% unsecured into ~6.0-6.5% unsecured. 8.625% PLUS second-lien security = lender syndicate believed the unsecured market was closed to MATW. The single most concrete pre-cutoff distress fact.

rfm_tuples.R: On January 7, 2025, the Company entered into a definitive contribution agreement... to sell its interest in the SGK Brand Solutions business to a newly formed entity created by affiliates of Southern Graphics, Inc... the Company will receive $250,000 [thousand] in cash and $50,000 of preferred equity in the New Entity. In addition... a 40% interest in the common equity of the New Entity. [Q2 FY25 10-Q HFS:] Goodwill $218,049 / Total assets HFS $428,010 / Total liabilities HFS $102,364 / Net assets HFS $325,646.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A + B: claim_evolution between 10-K (Nov 2024) and Q2 FY25 10-Q (Apr 2025). (A) Sale price vs book value. (B) Cross-reference to FY24 EY Critical Audit Matter that flagged SGK fair value only 7% above carrying value -- did the sale price 'confirm' the thin cushion?
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q2 FY25 10-Q Note 15 + 10-K Note 23 Goodwill + EY Critical Audit Matter
rfm_tuples.M_value: Total consideration $300M for net assets HFS $325.6M = sale BELOW carrying value. Only $250M is cash; $50M preferred equity + 40% retained common in private JV = limited liquidity; realized cash ~83% of carrying value. EY CAM had flagged SGK fair value only 7% above carrying as of Jan 1, 2024 ($218M of goodwill HFS). The sale crystallizes the thin cushion. MATW takes minority position (40%) -- losing operational control of a $530M-sales business with no buyer competition disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A + B convergence. Claim evolution from 'SGK is a strategic segment' (FY24 10-K) to 'SGK is held-for-sale at sub-carrying value' (Q2 FY25 10-Q) within 4 months is a quintessential lying-detector tell. Thin 7% cushion the auditor flagged was real and management knew it; selling below net book to a presumably-friendly buyer in the middle of an active proxy contest raises governance questions.

rfm_tuples.R: [Q2 FY25 10-Q MD&A:] '...$4.9 million of costs related to the Company's 2025 contested proxy...' [forward-looking:] '...the Company's plans and expectations with respect to its Board...'
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: governance_distress_tell. Activist proxy contests during the same six-month window as (a) a distressed refi and (b) a major divestiture are an extremely strong cluster signal. Cross-check 10b5-1 amendments and Form-4 activity.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q2 FY25 10-Q Item 2 MD&A + Item 5 + Q1 FY25 10-Q Item 5
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both 10-Qs explicitly state 'no director or executive officer adopted, modified, or terminated any Rule 10b5-1 trading arrangement' during Q4 cal-2024 or Q1 cal-2025 -- Mode A PASS on insider trading orderliness. HOWEVER, activist proxy costs ($4.9M in 6 months, very large for ~$650M market cap) + SGK divestiture + Sept '24 distressed refi + Mar '25 ATM = four-event distress cluster compressed into six months. CEO Bartolacci (since Oct 2006, age 64) and CFO Nicola (since Dec 2003, age 64) are both long-tenured; no transition disclosed pre-cutoff.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: four-event cluster is statistically anomalous for a 'no fundamental problem' issuer. Orderly 10b5-1 disclosure prevents outright red flag, but lack of disclosed CEO/CFO succession during active proxy contest is itself a tell -- management defending their seats rather than orderly-transitioning.

rfm_tuples.R: On March 11, 2025, in connection with the filing of an automatic shelf registration statement on Form S-3... the Company entered into an Equity Distribution Agreement for an At-The-Market equity offering program ('ATM Program') where the Company may issue and sell, from time to time, up to 1,250,000 shares of its Class A Common Stock... The Company has no near-term intention to utilize the ATM Program.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: capital_allocation_tell + equity_dilution_optionality. Companies that file ATMs at trough multiples are signaling (a) debt markets are closed/expensive and (b) they expect to need cash. 'No near-term intention' is boilerplate disclaimer.
rfm_tuples.M_source: Q2 FY25 10-Q Note 7 Debt and Financing Arrangements
rfm_tuples.M_value: 1.25M shares at ~$25 = ~$31M of potential issuance, ~4% dilution. Shelf filed at a near-multi-year low (down ~34% YTD). Treasury repurchases $4.4M H1 FY25 (vs Q4 FY24 buybacks $2.5M), but simultaneous ATM filing makes the buybacks optical rather than economic. Dividend MAINTAINED at $0.25/q ($1.00 annualized vs $0.96 FY24) -- nominal raise but not cut.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode B: ATM at multi-year low + near-flat dividend + distressed refi = 'we want optionality to dilute holders to repair the balance sheet.' Anti-correlated with management conviction in recovery. ANDE contrast: ANDE had a $100M buyback authorization barely touched (anti-dilution); MATW has an ATM (pro-dilution optionality).

Tesla is the LARGEST customer of Industrial Tech's dry-electrode business ('the Company's largest energy storage customer, which may be impacted by continuing disputes with such customer' -- Q2 FY25 10-Q MD&A). Both Tesla complaints + arbitration mean Industrial Tech's growth story is structurally impaired: 6% of consolidated sales is in active litigation with its own customer.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Mode A confirms dispute is escalating not resolving (second complaint, arbitration, legal-cost +39%). Mode B: 'largest energy storage customer' language in Q2 10-Q is a forced disclosure NOT in the FY24 10-K -- the claim drift confirms Tesla is BOTH disputant AND customer concentration. Highest-discrimination Mode B finding in the file.

Size small ($3.1M) but pattern -- MATW capitalizing a private vehicle run by a former insider, then writing to zero -- is governance optic overlapping with the activist proxy narrative.

Combined with long-tenured CEO (Bartolacci, 19y) and CFO (Nicola, 22y), the 'Liquid X' pattern is exactly the kind of fact a proxy challenger would highlight.

supplemental_signals.control_assertion: MATW is a STRESS-TEST NEGATIVE-CONTROL for the honesty-alpha framework. Forward return +29.4% means market eventually reversed the drawdown -- a SHORT-tier composite would have HURT the strategy. But the pre-cutoff distress cluster (distressed second-lien refi pricing, SGK sub-carrying-value sale, Tesla-litigation customer concentration, ATM at trough, capex cut, negative operating cash flow) is materially worse than ANDE. The fair score is NEUTRAL with mild distress tilt -- not deep-PASS and not deep-SHORT. Framework's correct call: 'high uncertainty, not deep-pass'.

summary: MATW is the canonical 'honestly disclosed multi-front distressed restructuring' case. Pre-cutoff filings reveal a tight distress cluster: (1) Sept 2024 distressed refinancing of 5.25% unsecured 2025 notes into 8.625% senior secured SECOND LIEN 2027 notes (+337 bps spread blowout with security ratchet) -- the most concrete Mode A tell that the unsecured market was closed to MATW; (2) FY24 GAAP net loss of $(59.7)M (second loss in 3 years) with $33.6M of goodwill+asset writedowns including Olbrich goodwill written to ZERO 2 years post-acquisition; (3) Jan 7, 2025 SGK Brand Solutions divestiture for $300M total consideration vs $325.6M net assets HFS -- effectively crystallizing the 7% goodwill cushion EY had flagged as a CAM and shrinking the company by ~30% of revenue; (4) active activist proxy contest with $4.9M of legal fees in H1 FY25; (5) Tesla litigation expanding (second complaint Feb 13, 2025) against the 'largest energy storage customer' in the dry-electrode growth story; (6) ATM equity shelf filed Mar 11, 2025 (1.25M shares ~4% dilution at trough); (7) capex guidance cut from $50-60M to $40-50M between filings; (8) operating cash flow flipped from +$29.8M (H1 FY24) to -$18.7M (H1 FY25); (9) revolver drawn balance creep from $410.5M to $495.0M. Honesty-offsets: EY clean Big-4 audit (since 2016) with a prescient CAM on SGK and effective ICFR; every distress event disclosed in real time (no concealed body); no 10b5-1 amendments in either pre-cutoff 10-Q. Verdict: NEUTRAL with distress tilt -- NOT a deep-PASS like ANDE but also not a strong SHORT because management was candid throughout. Pre-cutoff fact pattern would score composite ~0.45-0.55. Forward return +29.4% (positive control) means the framework should NOT issue a strong SHORT here; the honest reading is that MATW is in a genuine restructuring and the forward return reflects either successful execution of the SGK divestiture and proxy resolution, or macro/sector tailwinds masking continued underlying impairment.
